messages:
Maya Singh: flagging a permissions bug — I just saw a junior engineer trigger a canary rollout from the UI but they don't have rollout rights according to our role matrix.
Ethan Park: yikes. which user and when?
Maya Singh: user=julia.kim, ts=1711067845, deploy-service logs show grant: true for route /rollouts/start even though julia only has deploy.read and deploy.execute.
Jordan Lee: looking at last week's RBAC refactor PR (#502), mapping table changed: ops.rollouts -> rollout.manage, but some middleware still expects ops.rollouts. possible mismatch.
Sanjay Rao: quick grep in deploy-service: enforcement uses `required = config.get("required_perm")` and later `if required in user.perms: allow` — when required_perm is missing the default is empty string which empircally returned true in our legacy check.
Maya Singh: also noticed KMS audit stream has a gap — decrypt events for rollout-config key not present during the window 1711067000-1711068200.
ComplianceBot: AUDIT ALERT: Missing KMS.decrypt events for key=projects/redwood/keys/rollout-config between 2024-04-25T14:10:00Z and 2024-04-25T14:40:00Z.
Ethan Park: root cause hypothesis: (1) RBAC mapping typo allowed unintended access; (2) KMS audit hook absent for the path that builds rollout payloads.
Jordan Lee: agreed. plan to mitigate: 1) toggle UI controls for canary start/stop behind strict role check; 2) patch middleware to default-deny and match on any of [rollout.manage, ops.rollouts, rollout.admin]; 3) emit KMS audit events with key_id + principal for all decrypt ops.
Maya Singh: can someone flip the UI toggle in staging? `kubectl -n staging set env deployment/console CANARY_ENABLE=false`
Sanjay Rao: done in staging, verified julia cannot see start button. Also removed pending canary job from queue.
Ethan Park: working on hotfix: middleware change + unit tests. adding assertion that required_perm must not be empty and that default is deny. will push in ~30m.
Jordan Lee: I'll open an infra-keys ticket to ensure audit pipeline accepts new fields. tagging Infra-Keys. @Infra-Keys any blockers to adding key_id+principal fields?
Infra-Keys: no blockers, please include schema fields: `kms_key_id`, `caller_service`, `request_id`. We'll whitelist and route to the compliance pipeline.
ComplianceBot: NOTE: once events emitted, request a backfill for the missing window.
Maya Singh: mitigation checklist for incident notes: - Hotfix deployed to canary cluster - UI hidden for non-admins in prod until signoff - KMS audit hooks added and verified - Backfill requested + compliance notified - Add RBAC mapping smoke test to CI
Sanjay Rao: patch landed in staging (commit 9c8b), with e2e that simulates a user lacking rollout perms. Also added logging: `audit.emit("kms.decrypt", {...})` whenever rollout config key is used.
Ethan Park: deployed hotfix to canary cluster at 14:36 UTC. verified unauthorized user blocked and audit event emitted.
Maya Singh: severity: medium (internal privilege escalation risk). customer impact: none observed. recommend 2FA for any runtime-config changes while we complete postmortem.
Jordan Lee: followups: - PR to add static check that maps in RBAC-refactor PRs include a tests/mappings.yaml entry - run a one-off backfill job for 1711067000-1711068200 - update runbook entry for rollout permission changes
Infra-Keys: KMS backfill queued; ETA ~2hrs.
ComplianceBot: EVENT: KMS.decrypt events for deploy-service now being forwarded to compliance pipeline.
Maya Singh: I'll draft a short postmortem and assign owners for actions. tagging @Sanjay @Ethan for remediation.
Ethan Park: will monitor deploy logs for 48h and set alert: any /rollouts/start by non-admin triggers sec-eng pager.
Sanjay Rao: added alert rule and Slack webhook to #incidents.
Maya Singh: thanks team. when can we re-enable UI for production?
Ethan Park: target is after backfill + successful staging canary run + CI RBAC test merge — estimate 4-6 hours. will update here.
Maya Singh: closing for now, keeping incident thread open for updates. :shield:
